Users gave us the insight - when one use case outweighs the others, everything else seems like noise. We listened. Applied Intuition is bringing Physical AI to the machines that build, feed, and power the world. As Hardware Systems Lead for Industrials, you will be the hands-on chief engineer for the hardware that runs on heavy industrial vehicles in mining, agriculture, and construction. You will understand the full system, mechanical and electrical, and own the question that matters most in these environments: will it survive? - Lead integration of sensors (lidar, radar, cameras, GNSS/IMU), compute, power, networking, and actuation onto OEM heavy equipment

- Understand the host machine (powertrain, electrohydraulics, vehicle electrical architecture, CAN/J1939) well enough to integrate safely and reliably

- Be the technical authority and escalation point for hardware tradeoffs across mechanical, electrical, software, and test

- Lead hardware design reviews, set engineering standards, and mentor other engineers

- Support field deployments and commissioning at mine sites, farms, and customer facilities

AST SpaceMobile is seeking a skilled and detail-oriented 5-Axis CNC Programmer to support precision manufacturing operations within our satellite production facility. This role is responsible for developing, optimizing, and maintaining CNC programs for complex aerospace components using 5-axis machining centers. The ideal candidate will have strong experience with multi-axis CNC programming, machining strategies, tooling selection, blueprint interpretation, and precision manufacturing processes in a fast-paced production environment.

The 5-Axis CNC Programmer will collaborate closely with manufacturing engineers, machinists, quality teams, and production leadership to ensure parts are produced accurately, efficiently, and in compliance with engineering specifications and aerospace quality standards. Responsibilities include creating and modifying CNC programs, supporting machine setup and troubleshooting, optimizing cycle times, validating tooling paths, and assisting with continuous improvement initiatives to maximize machining performance and production efficiency. Strong knowledge of GD&T, CAD/CAM software, tooling, feeds and speeds, and precision measurement practices is highly preferred.

Hourly Pay Rate: $45.00 -$55.00/hr

$10,000 sign on bonus to assist with relocation.

Work Schedule

• Standard: Monday-Thursday (4x10 schedule aligned with AST operations)

• Overtime as required based on production demands

This role ensures all parts are manufactured in compliance with engineering specifications, quality standards, and production schedules in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

What you'll do:

Machine Programmer /Operation & Setup

• Program and Operate 5-axis CNC machines to manufacture complex aerospace components with tight tolerances

• Perform machine setup including tooling, fixtures, offsets, and work holding

• Load and verify CNC programs, ensuring correct parameters and material selection

🛠️ ABOUT OUR ENGINEERING TEAMS

Wayve’s engineering teams are building the AI, robotics, simulation, data, and systems foundations needed to deploy a generalisable AI Driver safely and at scale.

ABOUT THE VEHICLE GENERALIZATION TEAM

Vehicle Generalization makes it efficient, scalable, and predictable to deploy Wayve’s autonomous driving stack across a wide range of vehicle platforms by making our core autonomy generalise as widely as possible.

We work across pre- and post-training to improve how well our AI models generalise zero-shot to changes in perception-including cameras, intrinsics, field of view, lens distortion, and calibration-and embodiment, including vehicle dynamics, actuation limits, and rig geometry. We also own the Generalization Benchmark, Wayve’s tool for measuring how models transfer across platforms. Our work goes into production programmes with major OEMs.

We’re looking for a hands-on Machine Learning Engineer with a strong robotics background who understands how a real vehicle senses, estimates its state, and moves. You’ll identify where our models break down across platforms, understand why, and address those failures in training-then prove the improvement through rigorous evaluation.

🧠 YOUR DAY-TO-DAY

- Design and train models that are robust to differences between vehicles, using approaches such as conditioning or augmentation for vehicle kinematics and camera parameters.

- Create benchmarks and metrics for cross-platform performance, translating results into clear decisions for model and platform teams.

- Help root-cause on-road issues such as late turns, lane-keeping, and steering problems. Work with controls, calibration, and OEM engineers to separate model problems from system problems and identify the highest-impact model improvements.

- Move research into production in collaboration with Driving Core and application engineering teams.

- Support customer programmes, with some travel.

- Mentor teammates and help raise the bar for ML engineering across the team.

🧩 WHAT YOU’LL BE WORKING ON

- Pre- and post-training methods that improve zero-shot transfer across vehicle platforms.

- Robustness to changes in camera configuration, calibration, vehicle dynamics, actuation limits, and rig geometry.

- The Generalization Benchmark and metrics that measure how models transfer between platforms.

- Real-world, multi-sensor driving data and the interaction between sensors, data, models, and actuation.

- Production deployment of Wayve’s autonomy stack with major OEM partners.

🙌 YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

- You have several years of experience building and shipping ML systems in PyTorch and Python, including training at scale, debugging experiments, and rigorous evaluation.

- You have a strong robotics or automotive background in areas such as state estimation, sensor fusion, calibration, vehicle dynamics, or controls.

- You bring a systems perspective and can trace a problem through sensors, data, models, and actuation.

- You have experience working with real-world, multi-sensor driving or robot data.

- You communicate clearly across teams and are comfortable owning ambiguous problems from start to finish.

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience with end-to-end or learned driving and planning policies, imitation learning, or reinforcement learning.

- Experience with platform bring-up or deployment across multiple vehicles.

- C++ skills and experience with on-vehicle or embedded deployment.

Together for Girls works around the world and combines state-of-the-art data with powerful advocacy to end violence against children and adolescents, especially sexual violence. As the host of the Brave Movement, a survivor-led global advocacy initiative, we support and mobilize survivors and allies worldwide to drive political will, influence policy, and ensure that inaction is not an option.
By connecting the dots between understanding the problem, identifying effective solutions, tracking progress, and getting solutions into the hands of those with the power to make change, TfG amplifies our impact and drives toward the ultimate goal of creating a safer world for children and adolescents.
We are rooted in the conviction that violence is preventable and chance is possible, drawing upon 19 years of data from the Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS), new and emerging science, and lived experience. The Safe Futures Solutions Hub shares evidence and practice-based knowledge to inform effective prevention and response efforts, ensuring access to proven solutions across sectors. The Out of the Shadows Index tracks countries’ progress in addressing violence, providing an accountability framework and benchmark for advocacy. Brave Movement members and other activists leverage these tools to transform evidence into collective action for prevention, healing, and justice.
We are a nimble and highly impactful team that continues to grow and evolve. We work with a broad range of organizations, researchers, and advocates to drive change.
